verdict.rationale: Context-Aware Access is documented as creating granular access policies for apps based on attributes including 'device security status'. Community reports corroborate that it is enforced at login via Endpoint Verification, with non-compliant browsers rejected. The docs do not spell out the specific posture checks the story names. Admin troubleshooting is reported as painful because the denial page does not say which policy blocked access. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that managed status, disk encryption and screen lock are evaluable conditions, documented policy-evaluation details, and clear denial diagnostics.

support.subject: As a security engineer, only healthy devices get in — device posture (managed, encrypted, screen-locked) is checked in the auth policy before an app session is granted

citations.quote: you can create granular access control security policies for apps based on attributes, such as user identity, location, device security status, and IP address
With Google endpoint management, you can make your organization's data more secure across your users' mobile devices, desktops, laptops, and other endpoints.
